sources.quote: The earthquakes ratcheted up in 2022, and since then, 35 earthquakes with a magnitude of 2.5 or more have struck northwestern Louisiana.
sources.searcher_note: Names Red River Parish M4.9 and ties the rise to saltwater disposal; dates the rise to 2022 across all of northwestern Louisiana, not the lead's box or 2024 start.

sources.quote: Since December, at least 14 earthquakes with a magnitude greater than 2.5 have been detected in north Louisiana, according to the U.S. Geological Survey. The most significant occurred on March 5 near Coushatta and measured magnitude 4.9.
sources.searcher_note: University release: count since December 2025, M4.9 near Coushatta, M4.4 on March 9; also says a Tulane array was installed in October.

sources.outlet: Louisiana Department of Conservation and Energy
sources.quote: USGS has previously reported a number of earthquakes in the area since December 2025, with an overnight series of four Sunday night ranging in magnitude from 3.1 to 4.4.
sources.searcher_note: State regulator release on the Red River Parish series; says no clear-cut connection to injection found so far.

sources.quote: According to the U.S. Geological Survey, there was one in the morning that measured 2.5 and another one in the afternoon that shook the area at a 3.5 magnitude.
sources.searcher_note: Earliest coverage found: January 2024 Red River Parish quakes (M2.5, M3.5, another on Jan. 11); a geologist attributes them to the Red River fault, fracking link unknown.

sources.quote: There have been a series of small earthquakes reported in Red River and neighboring DeSoto Parish in recent months.
sources.searcher_note: Post-cutoff: M3.4 near Edgefield in August 2026, five months after the M4.9 in about the same location.

sources.quote: USGS researchers attributed a series of earlier near-border earthquakes in the area to fracking and associated wastewater disposal.
sources.searcher_note: Covers the March 5 Coushatta M4.9 as a record quake under USGS investigation, with earlier Texas-Louisiana border quakes tied to fracking and disposal.

notes: Many outlets covered the M4.9 (2026-03-05) and the March 9 follow-on quakes, naming Red River Parish/Coushatta. No source found stating the lead's specific claim of zero M2.5+ quakes 2010-2023 in the box or the count of 29 since Jan 2024. The Advocate dates the rise to 2022 across northwestern Louisiana (35 M2.5+); Tulane and the state regulator count from December 2025. KTBS Jan 2024 shows M2.5 and M3.5 quakes in Red River Parish in Jan 2024, consistent with a 2024 start. Cause is unsettled in all sources: the state regulator found no clear-cut injection link; a 2024 geologist quote points to the Red River fault. Houston Chronicle original URL failed to load (bot wall); Yahoo syndicated copy used. The Advocate quote sentence verified by direct download.
